turns.agent_input: Please provide step-by-step instructions for converting the DOCX to PDF and emailing it using my local machine.

agent_response.response:
Here are step-by-step instructions for both tasks:

---

## Step 1: Convert DOCX → PDF

### Option A: LibreOffice (recommended, works on macOS/Linux/Windows)

**Install** (if not already installed):
```bash
# macOS
brew install --cask libreoffice

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install libreoffice

# Windows – download from https://www.libreoffice.org/download
```

**Convert:**
```bash
libreoffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir docs/ docs/customer_report.docx
```
This creates `docs/customer_report.pdf` in the same directory.

### Option B: Pandoc (lighter weight, but may lose complex formatting)
```bash
# Install
brew install pandoc        # macOS
sudo apt install pandoc    # Ubuntu/Debian

# Convert
pandoc docs/customer_report.docx -o docs/customer_report.pdf
```
> Note: Pandoc PDF output requires a LaTeX engine (`brew install basictex` or `sudo apt install texlive`).

### Option C: Microsoft Word (if installed)
- Open `customer_report.docx` in Word
- **File → Save As → PDF**

---

## Step 2: Email the PDF

### Option A: Using `mail` / `mutt` (Linux/macOS CLI)

**Install mutt:**
```bash
# macOS
brew install mutt

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install mutt
```

**Send:**
```bash
echo "Hi Bob, please find the customer report attached." \
  | mutt -s "Customer Report" \
         -a docs/customer_report.pdf -- \
         bob@example.com
```
> Note: `mutt` needs a working SMTP config. Add this to `~/.muttrc`:
> ```
> set smtp_url = "smtps://you@gmail.com@smtp.gmail.com:465/"
> set smtp_pass = "your-app-password"
> set from = "you@gmail.com"
> set realname = "Your Name"
> ```
> (For Gmail, use an [App Password](https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords), not your regular password.)

### Option B: Using Python (no extra install needed)

Save this as `send_report.py` and run it:

```python
import smtplib
from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart
from email.mime.text import MIMEText
from email.mime.base import MIMEBase
from email import encoders

# ── Configure these ──────────────────────────
SMTP_SERVER = "smtp.gmail.com"       # your mail provider's SMTP server
SMTP_PORT   = 587
SMTP_USER   = "you@gmail.com"       # your email
SMTP_PASS   = "your-app-password"   # app password (not regular password)
FROM_ADDR   = "you@gmail.com"
TO_ADDR     = "bob@example.com"
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────

msg = MIMEMultipart()
msg["From"]    = FROM_ADDR
msg["To"]      = TO_ADDR
msg["Subject"] = "Customer Report"

msg.attach(MIMEText("Hi Bob,\n\nPlease find the customer report attached.\n\nBest regards", "plain"))

with open("docs/customer_report.pdf", "rb") as f:
    part = MIMEBase("application", "octet-stream")
    part.set_payload(f.read())
    encoders.encode_base64(part)
    part.add_header("Content-Disposition", "attachment; filename=customer_report.pdf")
    msg.attach(part)

with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_SERVER, SMTP_PORT) as server:
    server.starttls()
    server.login(SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS)
    server.sendmail(FROM_ADDR, TO_ADDR, msg.as_string())

print("Email sent successfully!")
```

```bash
python3 send_report.py
```

### Option C: macOS Mail (GUI)
- Open **Mail.app** → **New Message**
- To: `bob@example.com`
- Subject: `Customer Report`
- Drag & drop `customer_report.pdf` into the message body
- Hit **Send**

---

```bash
# 1. Convert
libreoffice --headless --convert-to pdf --outdir docs/ docs/customer_report.docx

# 2. Email
echo "Hi Bob, please find the customer report attached." \
  | mutt -s "Customer Report" -a docs/customer_report.pdf -- bob@example.com
```
